articles.title: European football: Martínez double gives Inter comeback draw at Roma
articles.summary: Roma lead 2-0 after Manu Koné’s first-half double. Strasbourg fans abuse Rosenior; Salah hits hat-trick. Lautaro Martínez rode to Inter ’s rescue as the Serie A champions fought back from 2-0 down to force a 2-2 draw at Roma, in a meeting of what had been the last two sides with 100% records.
body: Manu Koné’s double had given Roma a 2-0 lead at half-time but for the second time in a week Cristian Chivu’s side, inspired by Martínez, showed mettle as the champions fought back from such a deficit.

After the announcement earlier in the day of the death of Sandro Mazzola at the age of 83, both sides paid homage to the former Inter and Italy playmaker prior to kick-off, with the Nerazzurri also sporting black armbands.
Roma raced out of the blocks as Koné sent them ahead with less than six minutes on the clock when he readjusted his body well to rifle home Nahuel Molina’s knockdown.

The champions had bounced back from being 2-0 down inside the opening 16 minutes at home to Udinese to emerge 5-3 winners on Monday. But Inter were not at the races for most of the opening period at the Stadio Olimpico as Paulo Dybala twice threatened to double the hosts’ advantage.

articles.title: Belmont Park is back: inside New York’s $555m bet on horse racing
articles.summary: The storied Long Island racetrack, rebuilt with a $455m state loan, is smaller, sleeker and designed for a changing audience. Can it create the public needed to sustain it? Henry Miller stood on the trackside apron of the new Belmont Park on Friday trying to decide what he thought of the place.
body: “It has to grow on me,” said Miller, a 59-year-old retired sanitation worker from Brooklyn’s Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood who has been coming to New York racetracks for 47 years. “For me, it’s too much concrete. I don’t think it’s as friendly as the old Belmont.”

He missed the familiar trees and the ivy-covered brick facades. He missed the old bar and grandstand. Most of all, he was still mourning Aqueduct, the ramshackle Queens racetrack that shuttered in June as part of the $555m experiment that has made the reimagined Belmont possible.
For the first time in more than three years, horses were racing at Belmont Park on Friday. But almost everything else about the 121-year-old race course just outside New York city limits had changed.

Inside, the aesthetic is almost aggressively modern: bright white walls, gleaming floors and long, clean expanses that feel more THX 1138 than old-school racetrack. As one Fox Sports production assistant could be overheard describing it: “It looks kind of like an airport, but it’s beautiful.”

articles.title: Gvardiol signals return to best at left-back for Man City
articles.summary: Josko Gvardiol's season last time out was disrupted by a serious injury but the defender now appears to be returning towards his best by helping Manchester City to an impressive start to the new campaign.
body: Following a 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal in August, City have recovered to win six straight games in all competitions and the Croatian has been part of a defence that has conceded just twice in their opening four Premier League games.
With new captain Ruben Dias and England international Marc Guehi beginning to form a solid partnership in central defence, Gvardiol has been deployed at left-back and making the position his own.
Enzo Maresca's side host Sunderland on Sunday (14:00 BST) in a game the manager has described as being their "toughest" so far this season "because of how good they are".

Victory against the Black Cats will maintain City's winning streak and send Gvardiol off on international duty with Croatia - who face England and Spain in the Uefa Nations League - in high spirits following World Cup disappointment in the summer as his country went out at the last-32 stage.

articles.title: Zidane’s next move as France coach may reveal the wizard behind the curtain | Jonathan Wilson
articles.summary: It is apt that the most perplexing football country will now be guided by the most enigmatic of leaders. Even in his playing days, Zinedine Zidane seemed unknowable. As a manager, the sense of distance has only grown.
body: France are perhaps the most perplexing football country: a squad that teems with such talent that a B team would be serious contenders at a World Cup, that reached three major finals under Didier Deschamps with a sense of unfulfilment, a team that progressed but rarely entranced, or at least didn’t until this summer’s World Cup, when they attacked with gusto and ended up overrun in midfield by Spain.
On Friday, the two come together as Zidane, for the first time, leads France in their Nations League fixture against Turkey, an enigmatic coach leading a mercurial squad.

Zidane is one of five coaches to have won the Champions League on three or more occasions, ranking alongside Bob Paisley, Pep Guardiola and Luis Enrique and behind only Carlo Ancelotti. He is the only manager to win three successive Champions Leagues and yet few would consider him one of the game’s elite coaches. In that spell he won one La Liga title.

articles.title: Holmberg rescues point for Arsenal but Manchester United off the mark in WSL
articles.summary: Arsenal were mightily relieved as a 95th-minute Smilla Holmberg volley rescued a point at home to a much-improved Manchester United side, but the draw will not be enough to eradicate concerns about how far behind the leaders Manchester City Renée Slegers’ team are slipping already and how…
body: A defiant Manchester United stunned the north Londoners as Eva Olid’s side claimed the first point of her tenure with a performance that defied all of the pre-match scripts, but it was very nearly a victory, had it not been for Holmberg’s last-gasp back-post finish from Leah Williamson’s deep, diagonal ball into the box, which finally broke the visitors’ stubborn resistance.

Widely criticised for their dismal displays in their opening two defeats against London City Lionesses and Chelsea, Manchester United were heavily tipped to struggle again at the Emirates but an encouraging defensive effort and an against-the-run-of-play Julia Zigiotti Olme strike gave them a precious lead in a display that will buy the former Hearts manager Olid plenty of time to continue working on her style on the training ground and quieten those doubting her.

articles.title: Carrick has faith in VAR despite derby error
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick still has faith in VAR despite the derby blunder that cost his side in their home defeat by Manchester City
body: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says he still has faith in the video assistant referee - but added that the apology for the error that led to their defeat in the Manchester derby does not mean much.
Referee's body Pro Ref issued a formal apology to United within three hours of the end of Manchester City 's 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

Neither VAR Matt Donohue nor his assistant Blake Antrobus have been selected for games this weekend after failing to spot City midfielder Enzo Fernandez clearly in an offside position and interfering with play before Erling Haaland's matchwinner for City.
Carrick was livid after the game, saying it was a "worrying" interpretation of the rules.

articles.title: Biltmore Championship Asheville aces first year with fans of all ages
articles.summary: Golf fans and novices spend a day at Biltmore Championship Asheville at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove on Sept. 19, the third round of the PGA Tour.
body: ASHEVILLE - At the peak of the Biltmore Championship Asheville, tee times were adjusted for storms expected in the afternoon. The impending weather didn't stop crowds from rallying around the golfers across 18 holes at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.

On Sept. 19, Catherine and Derek Bledsoe and their six-year-old daughter Phipps traveled from Maryville, Tennessee, nearly 2.5 hours from Asheville, to attend the third round of the inaugural PGA Tour event. It was a success, with plenty of things to do, see, taste and make part of their family's cherished memories.
"The players have been really good with the kids. One of them signed a golf ball and gave it to her. You don't see that at some of your other tournaments," Catherine Bledsoe said.

As the PGA Tour's first run, the mood remained light and festive, despite high temperatures that led fans to seek respite in the shade of trees and in hospitality tents. It didn't detract from the picturesque scene backing the professional men's golf competition.

articles.summary: A week ago, the picture at Manchester United looked bleak. Then on Saturday, victory was snatched away from them at Arsenal. But have we seen signs of improvement from Eva Olid's side?
body: A week ago, the picture for Manchester United looked a lot bleaker than it did at the full-time whistle on Saturday.
Regardless of the stoppage-time equaliser they conceded at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, United's performance marked a major sign of progress.
Defeats in their opening two matches, including a 5-0 thrashing by Chelsea, meant the list of questions for new manager Eva Olid seemed endless.
United were disorganised, lacking in identity and were wide open at the back as their new era under Olid began in disappointing fashion.

articles.title: Mercedes F1’s Vesti Reveals Surprise Toto Wolff Question for Him in Canada
articles.summary: Mercedes F1 reserve Frederik Vesti reveals Toto Wolff question to him in Canadian GP, as he expands on a radio channel just for handful of them. In the latest nu podcast hosted by Anthony Davidson involving Andrew Shovlin and Vesti, revealed a new detail from the Danish reserve driver about how…
body: Vesti joined midway in the session and dropped startling information. The Dane is often spotted on world feed standing beside Wolff, with deputy Bradley Lord is on the other side. In a discussion about radio and communication, Shovlin touched on a special channel of selected people.

Vesti affirmed that it is him, Wolff, James Allison (technical director) and Lord. The Dane highlighted how emotional it gets for the Mercedes F1 team boss, especially during fights between teammates Andrea Kimi Antonelli and George Russell – which has happened multiple times this year.

“Well, definitely tense, I think seeing two Mercedes cars battle like that is great for the sport,” said Vesti. “It’s not great for Toto’s and everyone else’s heart rate, I think. [The special radio channel,] it’s very emotional.

“It’s Toto, James (Allison), Bradley (Lord), and me. And we can definitely discuss quite a few things, but from my perspective, Toto has some questions regarding racing, like what, from a driver’s perspective, and that’s where I can add value to,” summed up Vesti.

articles.title: Warrington beat Hull KR to set up semi against Leeds as Hiku sees red
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves set up a Super League semi-final with Leeds Rhinos after a 35-12 victory over reigning champions Hull KR in their eliminator showdown at the Halliwell Jones Stadium.
body: It marks Warrington's first semi-final since 2024 after they missed out on the play-offs in 2025.
It also means Willie Peters' tenure as Robins head coach is now over after his reign which featured the history-making season in 2025 in which he won the Super League for the club for the first time.

The flashpoint of the game came early in the second half when Peta Hiku saw red for a punch on George Williams and the player advantage for Warrington eventually became too much for Hull KR to contend with.

Warrington had a narrow 12-6 lead at half-time thanks to a converted Ben Currie try, Ewan Irwin penalty and Matty Ashton's score. Hull KR hit back through a Joe Burgess wonder-try that was started by Arthur Mourgue to get themselves in the game.

articles.title: Georgia Tech Cracked The Code At Southern Showcase
articles.summary: Men’s Team Breaks the Ceiling. Georgia Tech’s men’s cross country team finally cracked the code at the Southern Showcase, securing a third-place finish that matches the squad’s best result in event history.
body: The depth on this roster is what makes the third-place finish so impressive. Alexander Arrambide finished 18th with a time of 24:21.1, while Joey Sandel notched 25th at 24:35.1. Finishes in 38th and 45th place respectively rounded out the scoring for Matt Castronuovo and Wyatt Windham. That Tech had its top-five runners in the top 50 demonstrates the team possesses the density to defeat anyone on any given Friday morning. This result confirms the program is no longer just participating; it is competing for the podium.

The women’s team also proved they belong in the conversation, finishing eighth overall with 231 points while securing two top-15 runners. Finishing 13th in the 5k with a time of 16:59.6, Claire Shelton was followed by Lottie Chappell who took 15th overall at 17:07.9. Highlighting a rare level of consistency, the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets note that only three teams had multiple runners inside that mark. A 17:36.1 time placed Stella Chambless 34th, while Maddie Jones and Sadie Honig secured 88th and 95th places.

articles.title: Coventry seal first PL win in 25 years at Forest amid VAR controversy
articles.summary: Coventry earned their first Premier League victory in 25 years after Jay Dasilva's winner and a controversial disallowed Nottingham Forest equaliser saw the promoted side win 1-0 at the City Ground.
body: Frank Lampard's side needed a late VAR intervention to end their long wait for victory after Forest substitute Igor Jesus saw an 86th-minute equaliser ruled out.
Referee Jarred Gillett was sent to the pitchside monitor, where he adjudged Jesus had fouled Caleb Yirenkyi before finishing from close range inside the area.

Questioned on the incident, Lampard told Sky Sports: "As you see on the replay, he has that little step on him which puts him off balance, and it's a foul...I think that's VAR reaching the right decision."

It was the second goal Forest have had disallowed at home by VAR this season after Neco Williams had a goal chalked off in the 0-0 draw against Tottenham. and Oliver Glasner said afterwards: "I don't want to talk about it, to be honest. The referee decided, but of course it's a bit of deja-vu."
